claims.text: Reported HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of 786 MPa.
Reported HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
Reported HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal compressive strain of 13.5%.
Existing data for HfZrTiTa0.53 provide limited information about tensile ductility.
The proposed intervention is approximately 50% cold rolling followed by a roughly 1200°C, 1-hour solution treatment and a roughly 500°C, 2-hour temper.
Cold rolling will introduce defects and refine the grain structure.
The high-temperature solution anneal will homogenize HfZrTiTa0.53 and produce a uniform phase distribution.
The low-temperature temper will precipitate fine Hf-rich phases at grain boundaries.
The Hf-rich grain-boundary precipitates will be ductile.
The complete treatment will leave an overall refined grain structure.
Hf-rich grain-boundary precipitates will relieve local stress concentrations during tensile deformation.
The precipitates will blunt crack initiation and slow crack propagation.
Stress relief and crack blunting will increase tensile uniform elongation.
Treated HfZrTiTa0.53 may achieve roughly 50% greater tensile uniform elongation, reaching about 20% or more, using 13.5% as the stated baseline.
The treatment will preserve yield strength near 786 MPa.
The treatment will preserve compressive strength near 1314 MPa.
The treatment will preserve impact-triggered energy release at a level similar to the reported performance.
The strong refractory matrix is responsible for the alloy's high strength and impact-triggered energy release.
The predicted tensile response applies at room temperature under quasi-static loading near a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
Performance at elevated temperatures or high strain rates remains unverified.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is explicitly identified as terminal strain in compression, but the predicted tensile uniform-elongation improvement is calculated relative to that value as though it were a tensile uniform-elongation baseline. The baseline simultaneously says tensile-ductility data are limited.
